title: July: Taking Inventory
coreMove: Inventory changes behavior when every object becomes evidence: count what you own, name the emotion it served, and remove exits that keep old habits available.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who keep buying replacements for hidden basics
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small purchase could protect the clutter pattern from inspection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the missing can opener to turn irritation into a full cabinet audit.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose clothes preserve older or imagined selves
exampleSpecs.stakes: sentimental fit can disguise very low real-world use
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let the 15 percent wardrobe reality challenge fit-based keeping.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who keep one private route back to an old coping tool
exampleSpecs.stakes: a single object can weaken a recovery boundary while looking harmless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat the bottle of rum as a relapse option, not neutral clutter.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who mistake backup buying for responsibility
exampleSpecs.stakes: duplicates can turn anxiety into storage pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use duplicate toiletries to separate preparation from soothed anxiety.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who carry undecided boxes through new homes
exampleSpecs.stakes: mobility can postpone decisions while feeling like progress
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how repeated moves reveal avoidance rather than resolve it.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse the easiest purge with completion
exampleSpecs.stakes: early relief can make deeper attachments harder to inspect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let the first large purge create relief without pretending the work is finished.
